articles.title: The UFC used to pay fighters to use social media #ufc
articles.description: Dana White didn’t just embrace social media—he pushed the UFC into it while other major sports leagues were holding their athletes back. Chael Sonnen explains how Dana encouraged fighters and employees to build their online presence, handing out video cameras, laptops, and even offering incentives for growing Twitter followings. Meanwhile, the NBA was reportedly warning its players to stay off the platform. That contrast helped set the UFC apart. By giving fans greater access to fighters and letting athletes connect directly with their audience, the UFC embraced a level of accessibility that many sports organizations were—and still are—hesitant to allow. In this clip, Chael breaks down how Dana White went against the grain, why that approach mattered to MMA’s growth, and how the sport’s connection with everyday fans became one of its defining strengths. Was social media one of the biggest reasons MMA grew into a global sport? Subscribe for more Chael Sonnen takes, UFC analysis, MMA stories, and behind-the-scenes insight. #ChaelSonnen #DanaWhite #UFC #MMA #SocialMedia #UFCNews #MMAHistory #UFCFighters

articles.title: Gaethje's Two Options: Retire or Fight Arman
articles.description: Justin Gaethje has been crushing it lately, and Chael Sonnen says the words matter more than ever. Gaethje doesn't play the media game, he just tells the truth, and what he said on his recent media tour stopped Chael cold: bring me something new, or don't call until next year. The hardest "something new" at lightweight? Arman Tsarukyan, dangerous for his skills and for the unknown. Asked whether his future really comes down to two scenarios, walking away or fighting Arman, Gaethje said yes, those are the two options. He didn't accept the fight on the spot. Chael breaks down why the words themselves are the story, from Islam Makhachev's "anyone who makes weight" standard to the toughest-kid-in-school rule, and why Gaethje just handled his moment exactly the way you'd hope a champion would. 00:00 Gaethje is crushing it 00:08 He doesn't play the game 00:50 The champion's constitution 01:05 Islam's standard: anyone who makes weight 02:08 When Islam said no to Topuria 03:12 "Bring me something new" 03:33 Why Arman is the hardest fight 04:20 The media tour 04:36 Retire or Arman: those are the options 05:29 The toughest kid in school 06:31 Why words matter (the Jones lesson) 08:11 The Khabib code #ChaelSonnen #MMA #UFC #JustinGaethje #ArmanTsarukyan

articles.title: One Knockdown Doesn't Win a Fight
articles.description: Yoel Romero vs Darren Till was one of the highlights of the weekend, and the debate afterward missed the point. Chael Sonnen gives newer fans a history lesson on PRIDE rules, where fights were judged as one long war, then explains why the fight's only knockdown, scored by Romero, doesn't decide anything under either boxing or MMA scoring. Till was more aggressive, controlled the ring, and did more damage. The right guy won, and Chael says even under PRIDE rules the verdict wouldn't change. Plus: what makes Romero terrifying, why he gives away early rounds, and why Till, now thriving in boxing, shouldn't look back on his MMA run with regret. 00:00 Romero vs Till delivered 00:30 The PRIDE rules lesson 01:47 The knockdown and the "high spot" theory 02:00 Knockdowns in boxing 02:41 The three-knockdown rule 03:27 Cruz proved the point 03:47 Judge it by the ruleset 04:01 Why Till won 04:17 What makes Romero scary 05:13 "At some point he's coming" 05:43 When Romero looks tired, run 06:17 Till loves boxing 06:26 What's next for Till 07:47 The right guy won #ChaelSonnen #MMA #Boxing #UFC #DarrenTill #YoelRomero

articles.title: Dana vs Hearn Is the Real Fight
articles.description: Chael Sonnen is not ready to turn on Eddie Hearn, and he has been trying for two years out of loyalty to Dana White. With Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua on the horizon, Hearn insists Dana cannot be involved, citing contract language in the very first paragraph. Dana says he is promoting the fight. Chael explains why both men are telling the truth, why "promote" and "co-promote" mean very different things, and why the business of boxing is understood by maybe five men on earth. The twist: in North America, the Dana vs Hearn feud is drawing more attention than Fury vs Joshua itself, and Netflix may end up playing judge. articles.title: How technology has changed the fighting industry #ufc
articles.description: Why was it easier for some fighters to dominate for years in the past—and why is it so difficult to do that in modern MMA? Chael Sonnen explores how technology has transformed combat sports, from the days when fans gathered around radios to today’s world of endless fight footage, instant replays and detailed scouting. He explains how limited access to film once gave champions a major advantage. Fighters with unusual styles, like Lyoto Machida and Stephen Thompson, could present opponents with problems that were difficult to solve without extensive footage or specialized training partners. But now, every fight can be studied, every mistake analyzed and every technique prepared for. Chael breaks down how the evolution of technology has changed the challenge of staying champion—and why the sport’s most unique fighters may have had an even greater advantage in the past. #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #LyotoMachida #StephenThompson #MMAHistory #UFCChampions #FightAnalysis

articles.title: Why Chael Sonnen hates when fighters pull out of fights #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen’s UFC journey almost started with his mother trying to bribe Joe Silva for a contract. Chael tells the story of how badly fighters wanted UFC opportunities back in his era. There was no asking about the money or worrying about whether the matchup was ideal—they just wanted the chance to compete. So badly, in fact, that Chael’s mother came up with a plan to offer Joe Silva $50,000 to get her son a UFC contract. And the proposed debut? Heavyweight. Against Andrei Arlovski. Chael says he was willing to take the fight despite knowing exactly how dangerous that matchup could be. It’s a completely different perspective on fighting than what Chael sees today, when fighters are regularly offered multiple opportunities each year and sometimes pull out because of weight, circumstances or other concerns. Chael explains why that old-school mentality still shapes the way he views fighters today. #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #AndreiArlovski #UFCHistory #MMAHistory #JoeSilva #UFCStories

articles.title: Gable Steveson Doesn't Belong in the UFC?
articles.description: The media is dancing on Gable Steveson's grave after a 12-second knockout, and Chael has had enough of it. In this video, Chael dismantles the narrative that Gable "doesn't belong in the UFC." The fight lasted exactly 12 seconds, the same duration as Jose Aldo versus Conor McGregor, and nobody ever said Aldo didn't belong. Gable had already won a fight in the UFC before this loss, proving he earned his spot. Chael draws a sharp comparison to Olympic boxing, where a gold medalist walks into the professional ranks in the top 10 with zero pro fights, which is essentially what Gable did transitioning to MMA. He revisits the bare-knuckle knockout that prompted Joe Rogan to text Dana White saying the whole division was in trouble, and reminds everyone that Gable has bounced back before, including from the biggest upset in wrestling history in the NCAA final in front of the President on ESPN. Chael's core argument is simple: nobody could have taken that shot, just like nobody could have taken what Masvidal did to Askren. But the real kicker is this, not one UFC fighter under contract has called Gable out, even though fighting him guarantees a main card spot, a press conference, and maximum attention. Everybody is certain he doesn't belong, yet nobody has asked for the shot. Whatever Gable does next, we're all going to be watching. Subscribe for daily MMA breakdowns and Chael's unfiltered take on the fight game. #MMA #UFC #GableSteveson

articles.title: Ilia Topuria’s 145 Return Isn’t Happening Yet #ufc
articles.description: Is Ilia Topuria going back to 145 pounds? Chael Sonnen has an emphatic answer: **not anytime soon.** Justin Gaethje recently suggested that Ilia is naturally a 145-pound fighter and argued that size could eventually become an issue for him at lightweight. But Chael believes Ilia’s mindset makes a return to featherweight extremely unlikely right now. According to Chael, Ilia won’t simply leave lightweight because the division is physically demanding. He believes Ilia will stay at 155 until he solves the problem—and that means winning the UFC lightweight championship. A return to 145 could still happen eventually, especially if it means a massive matchup with Alexander Volkanovski. But Chael believes there is one major condition: Ilia would first need to recapture the lightweight title. So forget about an immediate move back to featherweight. If Chael is right, Ilia Topuria is staying at 155. #UFC #MMA #IliaTopuria #ChaelSonnen #UFC155 #UFC145 #AlexanderVolkanovski #JustinGaethje #UFCNews

articles.title: The real reason Chael Sonnen lost to Anderson Silva #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen reveals one of the strangest moments of his fighting career—and it happened because his corner told him the wrong round. Chael had never fought five rounds before, and as he entered the later stages of the fight, he was running on exhaustion, fear and urgency. His mindset was simple: get the takedown, stay busy and keep scoring. Then his corner told him it was the fourth round. The problem? It was actually the fifth. Suddenly, the urgency disappeared. Chael no longer believed he needed to keep attacking—he thought he still had another round to work. Instead of fighting to win, he was unknowingly fighting to beat the clock. Chael explains how that experience changed his perspective on five-round fights and why the mental side of championship rounds can be just as important as the physical exhaustion. Was it an excuse? Maybe. But Ch

articles.title: Should Arman Be Ranked Above Ilia?
articles.description: The new MMA Fighting rankings just put Arman Tsarukyan ahead of Ilia Topuria, and Chael is not sure they got it right. In this video, Chael breaks down one of the most surprising ranking debates in recent memory. Ilia Topuria is a two-division UFC champion in the two hardest weight classes in the sport, a feat only Conor McGregor had accomplished before. Chael argues that if not for paperwork, Ilia would have simultaneously held the featherweight, lightweight, and BMF titles. He compares Ilia's resume to Islam Makhachev's, noting both have one loss and two-division championships, and questions whether recency bias is clouding everyone's judgment. Chael also dives into the bizarre narrative that Topuria shouldn't even qualify for a title shot at the belt he held just five months ago. This is Chael at his best, using history, logic, and a little bit of mischief to challenge how we think about greatness. He asks fans to imagine looking back five years from now with fresh eyes: would you still rank Islam ahead of Ilia? It's a debate about paper versus perception, and Chael makes a compelling case that the rankings might be missing the bigger picture. Subscribe for daily MMA breakdowns and Chael's unfiltered take on the fight game. #MMA #UFC #IliaTopuria #ArmanTsarukyan

articles.title: Arman Tsarukyan Is NOT Underestimating Gaethje #ufc
articles.description: Arman Tsarukyan believed in Justin Gaethje when almost nobody else did—and Chael Sonnen says that could matter if they fight. Arman reportedly put $1 million on Gaethje to beat Ilia Topuria, showing just how highly he has rated Justin’s ability all along. That belief could become important in a matchup between the two. Chael explains why Arman is unlikely to make the same mistake other opponents have made: underestimating Gaethje. Justin’s ability to keep moving forward, absorb adversity and refuse to quit is one of his biggest weapons. Arman knows exactly what he’s dealing with. He knows Gaethje’s power, his leg kicks, his wrestling credentials and how difficult he is to control. That awareness could make this matchup completely different. Arman Tsarukyan believes in Justin Gaethje—and he knows exactly how tough he is. #UFC #MMA #ArmanTsarukyan #JustinGaethje #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #UFCLightweight #IliaTopuria #MMA

articles.title: Gane Called Tom Aspinall Mentally Fragile
articles.description: Ciryl Gane just called Tom Aspinall "mentally fragile" to his face, and Chael thinks the insult might reveal something much deeper about why Aspinall hasn't returned. In this video, Chael presents a fascinating theory about the power of the subconscious mind in fighting. Using the story of a roofer who couldn't bring himself to climb back on the same roof where he fell, and John Stossel's famous WWF lawsuit where Stossel admitted he felt better the moment the settlement check arrived, Chael draws a parallel to Aspinall's situation. Aspinall is out with an eye injury, and his reward for healing is a rematch with Gane, a nightmare matchup he already knows too well. Chael also revisits Jon Jones's surprising decision to step away rather than face Aspinall, and Jones's backhanded compliment that there's not enough footage of Aspinall to even form a game plan. This isn't just fight analysis, it's psychology. Chael explores how the mind can protect the body by inventing reasons to stay out, and why Gane's accusation that Aspinall is using the eye poke as an excuse might be both cruel and accidentally insightful. Whether Aspinall is truly hurt or subconsciously avoiding the fight, the question remains: what happens when he has no choice but to return against Gane? Subscribe for daily MMA breakdowns and Chael's unfiltered take on the fight game. #MMA #UFC #TomAspinall #CirylGane

articles.title: Why Would Morales Take This Fight?
articles.description: Michael Morales is one win away from fighting Islam Makhachev for the title, so why on earth did he just accept a fight with Ian Garry? In this video, Chael breaks down the high-stakes chess match happening at welterweight right now. Morales hasn't fought since November, stayed healthy, and stayed unbooked, which in the UFC usually means one thing: a title shot is coming. But after a heated back-and-forth with Ian Garry that spilled into the media, Morales said yes to a fight that could cost him everything. Chael explains the rumor about Dana White's whispered promise at Madison Square Garden, why the fans sided with another contender over Morales, and how Garry is the worst possible opponent to take right before a title fight. This is a masterclass in UFC matchmaking and risk management. Chael lays out why beating Garry does almost nothing for Morales, but losing to him ends the title dream instantly. It's the kind of fight that looks brave on paper and reckless in practice, and Chael isn't afraid to say so. Subscribe for daily MMA breakdowns and Chael's unfiltered take on the fight game. #MMA #UFC #MichaelMorales #IanGarry

articles.title: The Weirdest 4 Minutes in MMA
articles.description: Darren Till and Yoel Romero just stood nose-to-nose for four straight minutes, and Chael can't stop thinking about how bizarre the whole thing was. In this video, Chael breaks down the strangest face-off in recent memory, explaining why the staredown ritual exists in the first place and what really happens when the camera flashes finally stop. Drawing from his own fighting career, Chael admits he used to believe winning the face-off gave him an edge, until he realized it had absolutely no effect on the fight itself or how many people tuned in. He walks through the moment a UFC staffer finally taps you on the shoulder to end it, and the strange realization that once the lights stop flashing, that's just what you look like. This goes beyond Till and Romero. It's about the psychology of intimidation, the theater of fight promotion, and why two grown men get locked into a staring contest neither one can actually win. Chael's conclusion is blunt: once you're in it you might as well finish it, but don't lie to yourself that it means anything. Subscribe for daily MMA breakdowns and Chael's unfiltered take on the fight game. #MMA #UFC #DarrenTill #YoelRomero
